paper: OpenWAM: An Open Framework for Composable World-Action Models
claims_checked: Causal robot-video pretraining corpus (14,640 nominal hours, 3.34M trajectories, 32 B200 GPUs, 14 days, Wan2.2-5B adaptation)
MoT dual-stream architecture (Video Expert 5B hidden 3072, Action Expert 2B hidden 2048, 30 layers, 24 heads, head dim 128)
Four configurable interaction topologies (Joint, VTA, ATV, Decoupled) and flow matching formulation
Independent local-context dynamics interfaces (LC-IDM and LC-FDM) conditioned on (O_0, q_t, O+) or (O_0, q_t, A+)
LIBERO-Long-CF counterfactual benchmark (32,000 segments, 4.10M controls, 29.7x expansion, 7 intervention families)
Closed-loop policy evaluation on LIBERO (Spatial 98.6%, Object 99.4%, Goal 98.4%, Long 97.8%, Mean 98.6%)
Real-world dual Franka FR3 bimanual manipulation (Toast Bread 92.0%, Rubik's Cube 90.0%, Sort Cups 94.4%, Mean 92.1%)
Component transfer on four LIBERO-90 targets (Tasks 64, 74, 21, 45; frozen LC-IDM mixed reaching 84.0% mean success)
Forward dynamics prediction error (-34.5% MSE, K=16 outcome accuracy 21.1% -> 71.3%)
Multi-objective vs dedicated specialist dynamics trade-off compared with UVA
caveats: Real-world bimanual experiments evaluate native VTA and Joint policies; zero-shot dynamics transfer was primarily benchmarked in simulation due to real-robot counterfactual data collection cost
Multi-objective training (policy + IDM + FDM) displays expected trade-offs compared to single-purpose specialists (Table 14)
Inference acceleration (CUDA Graphs, DiT cache) represents engineering deployment mechanisms aligned with chunked streaming execution
